subject: ventures/mobile-tire-van-job-picker
professional: an owner-operator or dispatcher of a one-van mobile tire / roadside business, plus an operations-research practitioner who would check the exactness of the scheduling search

evidence.correctness: Ran `node cli.mjs plan fixtures/jobs.csv` (defaults): 8 of 10 jobs, $486.23, 86.2 mi, home 16:57; baselines $308.45 (6 jobs) and $127.33 (3 jobs); break-even prices $652.65 (Four new tires - truck) and $97.66 (Valve stem). Recomputed independently with a Python script (written for this audit, not the author's code) that enumerates every ordering of every subset (10P0..10P10, ~9.8M orders) with the documented cost model: best day 486.2253 over order (spare swap, sedan, SUV, fleet check, van flat, TPMS, trailer, rotation), home 1017.35 min = 16:57; forced-inclusion break-even 652.6538 and 97.6586; both greedy baselines 308.4536 and 127.3293. All match to the cent. Also ran a 14-job random queue: engine returns a plan in 1.2 s. Caveat: the cost model itself (see domain) is the author's; I verified the arithmetic and optimality of that model, not its fit to a real van.
evidence.completeness: Checked each README/page claim: CSV/stdin CLI with --start/--end/--hourly/--per-mile/--speed/--circuity/--json works; exact DP works (matches brute force); decline reasons and exact break-even prices work (verified); first-come and biggest-ticket baselines work; idle/waiting finding exists; 14-job cap enforced with a clear error; header/comment/12-hour time parsing works; browser page has worked example equal to the fixture, opt-out and usage counting; guide page and llms.txt exist. No TODO/stubs found. Not delivered but never claimed: traffic, second tech, job dependencies, cancellations (README lists them as out of scope).
evidence.verification: `node --test engine.test.mjs cli.test.mjs page.test.mjs usage.test.mjs`: 29 pass, 0 fail (engine tests include a 120-trial randomised comparison with brute force over every ordering of every subset, hand-arithmetic simulate test, parser line-number tests, page-vs-fixture and guide-vs-engine tests). Seeded mutation 1: added +1 minute to every job start in the DP extend() only (engine.mjs): 4 tests failed (caught). Seeded mutation 2: relaxed the latest-start check in the DP by 30 minutes: 4 tests failed (caught). Both reverted with git checkout; git status on the subject is clean. Gap: brute-force trials use n<=6 only, so the 7 to 14 job regime (the one users hit) relies on the same code path, not direct tests; no test of shifts crossing midnight or of the 14-job limit timing.
evidence.craft: Read engine.mjs, cli.mjs, README, VENTURE.yaml, llms.txt, page.test.mjs, engine.test.mjs. Clean pure-function engine, single source of truth for the page and CLI, exact DP with a dominance prune, EPS tolerances, input validation with line-numbered errors, no network. Defects: parseJobs splits on bare commas so a quoted CSV field (name with comma) is mis-parsed and a column count error or shifted columns result (documented only as 'avoid commas inside names'); header is detected only if first cell is 'name'; shift times past midnight are impossible (clock() mods 24h, shiftEnd must exceed start in same day); a declined, otherwise-feasible job has minPrice computed from forced.order which silently overrides the 'loses money alone' price (consistent but the reason text and number come from different calculations); sitemap.xml and robots.txt use relative URLs (invalid per sitemap protocol).
evidence.claims: Checked: exact optimum (verified by independent brute force); 'tests check it against every ordering of every subset' (true, n<=6); worked-queue numbers on the guide page ($308.45, $127.33, $486.23, 86.2 mi, 16:57, $177.77, $652.65, $97.66) all reproduced by the CLI and by my script, and page.test.mjs pins them; zero network and no upload (index.html imports only local usage.mjs; no fetch in engine/cli); no-warranty, not-advice, motor-club/safety caveat present on both pages and README; MIT licence file present. Weaknesses: llms.txt links point at the retired duncan-haywood.github.io address, not marisstella.app (stale); guide says the $55 valve stem is '15 miles out' but the fixture puts it 15 east and 12 north (about 19 mi straight-line, 25 road miles); 'Volume not measured' and all hypotheses are marked untested in VENTURE.yaml, which is honestly stated; stage is 'prototype'.
evidence.fitness: Walked a dispatcher's morning: they must convert every customer address to miles east/north of the depot by hand (no geocoding, no paste of addresses, no map), build a CSV, and enter hourly and per-mile costs, then read the plan. That coordinate step is the hardest part of the real job and is the main reason the tool is a demo-grade decision aid today. Also lacks arrival-time buffers or a 'must finish by' window, and does not re-plan as calls arrive during the day (the stated 'return each morning' use). Output itself is clear (route, times, decline reasons, quote price), the CLI and page both work. A real operator could use it for a few jobs but not as a daily workflow.
evidence.domain: Compared with how mobile tire and roadside operators and field-service dispatchers actually decide (price per job vs drive, time windows) and with the orienteering / TSP-with-time-windows formulation: the exact label-setting DP over (subset, last) with Pareto (time, profit) labels is the correct textbook approach for n<=14. Departures a practitioner would hit: (1) the hourly van-and-tech cost is charged on service and drive time but waiting is free, which treats a largely fixed wage/insurance cost as variable and can make a job 'lose money' that adds positive contribution to a day already paid for (stated in the model note but not offered as a switch); (2) constant 30 mph and a single circuity factor, no per-leg travel time variability or buffer, so a plan that gets home at 16:57 against a 17:00 limit is not robust; (3) service time is treated as deterministic. These are disclosed as limits, but a dispatcher would want a slack setting.

defects.what: Input requires hand-computed miles east/north per job; no address geocoding or map entry, so the intended user's real workflow stalls at data entry

No schedule slack/buffer setting: an optimal plan can finish with minutes to spare, and the hourly cost model charges fixed wages as variable cost, which can mislabel a positive-contribution job as 'loses money'
llms.txt page links use the retired duncan-haywood.github.io host instead of https://marisstella.app/mobile-tire-van-job-picker/
sitemap.xml and robots.txt Sitemap line use relative URLs, which the sitemap protocol does not allow
Naive comma split: quoted CSV fields with commas misparse; shifts crossing midnight are unsupported; brute-force test covers only n<=6
Guide says the valve stem is '15 miles out' though the fixture puts it at (15, 12), about 19 mi straight-line

verdict: The engine is exact and right: every headline number (plan profit, route finish, both baselines, both break-even prices) was reproduced to the cent by an independent exhaustive search over about 9.8 million orderings, the 29 tests pass, and two seeded mutations in the DP were caught. Claims on the page, guide and README are backed by files and pinned by tests, with a minor stale-host defect in llms.txt and a loose phrase in the guide. It is finished against what it says, so it meets the computed bar on correctness, claims and verification. It falls short as a practitioner's tool: the user must hand-convert addresses to east/north miles, there is no schedule slack, and the cost model treats fixed wages as variable. A senior dispatcher would accept the optimisation and not yet trust it as a daily workflow. Scores are before any fix.
